header: Date: 2026-05-21 | Time: 15:00-15:52 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Rishi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM); Emma Torres (Marigold Procurement), Liam O'Neill (Marigold Legal), Priya Rao (Marigold Security), Noah Brooks (Marigold Eng)
summary: Procurement and legal review covering MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations for Dedicated vs Hosted, pricing guidance for reserved capacity, SOC2 artifacts request, and next steps for procurement timeline and onboarding. Customer requested redlines and sizing/benchmarks before procurement sign-off.
topics: MSA redlines, DPA data residency and KMS, SLA/uptime and latency SLOs for Dedicated, Pricing for committed GPUs vs burst, SOC2 / ISO artifacts, VPC/Private deployment options, Onboarding timeline and PO flow
transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining - looks like we have a full room from Marigold, really appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Emma Torres: Hi, Emma here - head of procurement.
[00:15] Liam O'Neill: Liam - legal.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Priya, security.
[00:20] Noah Brooks: Noah - engineering.
[00:22] Alyssa Chen: Great, and from Redwood we've got Rishi and Jordan, Rishi's our solutions engineer, Jordan handles post-sale.
[00:30] Rishi Patel: Hey everyone.
[00:32] Jordan Kim: Hi, thanks for having us.
[00:36] Alyssa Chen: Agenda - MSA/DPA status, SLA asks, pricing and capacity, SOC2/artifact handoff, and next steps. We'll keep it focused.
[01:05] Emma Torres: Thanks. So procurement is ready to move but legal flagged some DPA language around data residency and delete requests. Also need clarity on who manages KMS and whether logs are retained.
[01:20] Liam O'Neill: Yep, on the MSA we have two main redlines - limitation of liability and the data-processing sections. For DPA, we want clear language on subprocessor list and cross-border transfers.
[01:35] Rishi Patel: Totally understood. For the KMS piece, Redwood offers both customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and our hosted KMS option, I think that's in the DPA appendix but we can make it explicit. We also have audit logs that can be exported to your SIEM.
[01:58] Priya Rao: Export to SIEM is important - can you confirm log retention window and format?
[02:05] Rishi Patel: Default retention is 90 days in the console, and we can provide daily exports in JSON or syslog streams to your S3/CloudWatch depending on the region.
[02:20] Noah Brooks: Are those logs tenant-scoped? We need separation between workloads.
[02:25] Rishi Patel: Yes, tenant-scoped. For Dedicated we give isolated pools and separate audit trails.
[02:40] Emma Torres: On SLAs - procurement wants an SLA that includes availability and a remedy structure, ideally credits. Can you walk through Redwood's SLA tiers?
[02:50] Jordan Kim: Sure. Hosted API has standard 99.5% uptime with credit tiers. Dedicated comes with an SLA tier we can negotiate for 99.9% or higher depending on reserved capacity and geographic redundancy. For Private (VPC/on-prem) we provide operational support SLAs but uptime is influenced by customer infra.
[03:20] Liam O'Neill: For us, anything less than 99.9% is a stretch - our customer SLAs demand high availability.
[03:33] Alyssa Chen: Understood. We can propose a 99.9% SLA for Dedicated with defined credits and playbook for incidents. We should capture what Marigold needs as the exact SLOs - is it per-region or global?
[03:50] Noah Brooks: Per-region - low latency in our EU region is critical.
[03:58] Rishi Patel: Good to know. We'll include region-specific SLOs. Also want to mention routing and fallback - we can route to compatible model variants in other regions if capacity is constrained, but that's an operational trade-off for latency.
[04:25] Emma Torres: Okay, demarcate that in the SLA doc.
[04:30] Liam O'Neill: Another legal point: indemnity cap and termination for convenience - we have standard language but want to tighten breach definitions.
[04:40] Alyssa Chen: We can work with legal on clean breach clauses. I'll send suggested wording.
[04:48] Priya Rao: On security, SOC2 reports - can you share the latest report and the control mapping? Also curious about encryption at rest and in transit, and whether private deployments retain full control of keys.
[05:05] Jordan Kim: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II report and an artifact pack. Encryption in transit is TLS1.2+, and encryption at rest uses AES-256. For Private deployments you can manage keys via customer KMS/HSM. We'll add that to the DPA exhibit.
[05:30] Emma Torres: Great. Procurement also asked about data residency and whether logs or models are stored outside EU.
[05:40] Rishi Patel: For EU-region deployments we keep models and data in the selected region unless you opt into cross-region features. We'll make explicit in the DPA that EU data stays in EU unless you request otherwise.
[06:00] Noah Brooks: Can we get written confirmation of that?
[06:04] Jordan Kim: Yes, we'll include a clause and an appendix stating region behavior.
[06:10] Emma Torres: Pricing - we need a committed capacity quote and a comparison to on-demand. We're looking at ~8M calls/mo - mostly short chat queries.
[06:25] Rishi Patel: For 8M calls/month (avg 30 tokens per call) we'd recommend a Dedicated pool with 8 A100-equivalent vGPU slots with burst to handle peaks. Pricing would be a reserved capacity discount - I'll send the sizing spreadsheet.
[06:45] Noah Brooks: How do you handle quantization and token costs? If we quantize models, do we lose accuracy?
[06:52] Rishi Patel: We provide quantization profiles and recommendations per workload. Some models lose a percentage of accuracy depending on tasks; we can run a small eval on your prompts. Quantization reduces VRAM and per-token cost.
[07:18] Liam O'Neill: Procurement will need the full price table and the cancellation penalties for reserved capacity.
[07:25] Alyssa Chen: We'll include termination and usage reconciliation terms in the pricing annex.
[07:30] Emma Torres: What's the onboarding timeline? We want to complete procurement and be live in prod in about 6 weeks.
[07:38] Jordan Kim: Typical onboarding for Dedicated is 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and VPC peering. If you go hosted first, you can start within a few days. For Private, add time for networking and KMS integrations.
[07:58] Priya Rao: We prefer Dedicated in our VPC with customer-managed KMS. Need to know firewall and IP allowlist requirements.
[08:08] Rishi Patel: We'll share the network runbook - ports, IPs, peering steps.
[08:14] Noah Brooks: Any standard pen test or security questionnaire?
[08:18] Jordan Kim: We have an exhaustive security questionnaire we can prefill and the SOC2 artifact pack.
[08:26] Emma Torres: On the MSA redlines - Liam, I sent you the baseline earlier. Are the redlines mostly standard?
[08:34] Liam O'Neill: Mostly yes, but a couple of commercial items and the data processing addendum need more clarity - particularly on subprocessors and breach notification timelines.
[08:48] Rishi Patel: For breach notification we do 72 hours for breaches that affect confidentiality. We can confirm notification to named contacts and provide timelines for forensic logs.
[09:00] Liam O'Neill: We prefer 48 hours if feasible.
[09:04] Alyssa Chen: I'll take that back and see what we can do - we may be able to improve notification SLA in the DPA for contractual customers.
[09:12] Priya Rao: Also need retainer for forensic assistance - is that billable?
[09:16] Jordan Kim: Standard support includes initial incident triage; extended forensic assistance can be scoped as part of a support package. We'll propose options.
[09:32] Emma Torres: Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a limited one-way indemnity for data breaches?
[09:38] Alyssa Chen: We'll need internal approvals but can propose a commercial compromise. I'll flag legal to follow up with Liam.
[09:46] Noah Brooks: On performance - Rishi, can you summarize expected latency for EU region on Dedicated for a 2k token chat?
[09:54] Rishi Patel: For 2k tokens on A100-equivalent Dedicated, tail latency under typical batching is around 500-900ms per token depending on batch size; end-to-end for a 2k token response typically 6-12 seconds, but we can tune with continuous batching and KV cache for chat workloads. There's variability based on model.
[10:18] Noah Brooks: That's reasonable. We need a benchmark run on our prompts.
[10:22] Rishi Patel: We'll schedule a benchmark run - I'll need a representative prompt set and sample inputs.
[10:30] Emma Torres: Procurement will also want a copy of the uptime credit formula and how it's applied to invoices.
[10:35] Jordan Kim: We'll attach the SLA credit schedule to the MSA exhibit and show examples.
[10:42] Liam O'Neill: For procurement, invoice terms and PO net-30 - is that standard?
[10:47] Alyssa Chen: Yes, net-30 is standard for enterprise. We can discuss payment terms in the order form.
[10:54] Priya Rao: A couple more security Qs - do you support customer-managed HSM for key rotation and audit?
[10:59] Rishi Patel: Yes, for Private and Dedicated VPC we support customer KMS/HSM integrations and key rotation.
[11:10] Emma Torres: Okay, let's talk deliverables. Alyssa, you said you'd provide redlined MSA. Can you confirm the date?
[11:16] Alyssa Chen: I can send redlines by Monday, 2026-05-24.
[11:20] Emma Torres: Good. Rishi - sizing spreadsheet due when?
[11:24] Rishi Patel: I'll get that out by Wednesday, 2026-05-26.
[11:28] Jordan Kim: And I'll share SOC2 and the security questionnaire by end of week.
[11:34] Liam O'Neill: We'll review and get back with any additional redlines. Procurement aiming to approve by 2026-06-04.
[11:40] Alyssa Chen: Excellent. Any blockers we haven't covered?
[11:46] Priya Rao: Only the SOC2 artifacts and network runbook.
[11:50] Noah Brooks: Also want a quick pilot - maybe a 2-week perf run in our EU region before full commit.
[11:55] Rishi Patel: We can do a pilot on hosted or dedicated staging - we'll size for the pilot in the spreadsheet.
[12:08] Emma Torres: Sounds good. Let's recap next steps and owners.
[12:14] Alyssa Chen: Recap: Alyssa will send MSA/DPA redlines (05/24), Rishi sends sizing & benchmark plan (05/26), Jordan sends SOC2 and runbook (05/28), Marigold to confirm procurement timeline (05/22). We'll schedule a pilot window after the sizing is approved.
[12:36] Liam O'Neill: One last legal note - please include a subprocessor list or a commitment to notify changes with 30 days notice.
[12:45] Alyssa Chen: Noted, we'll include subprocessor notice language.
[12:50] Emma Torres: Okay folks, thanks - we'll look out for the docs.
[12:54] Jordan Kim: Thanks everyone.
[12:58] Rishi Patel: Thanks all.
[13:02] Alyssa Chen: Bye.
[13:10] [call ended]
